statement: A.R.S. 16-551(C): early election board tallies 'shall not be released or divulged before all precincts have reported or one hour after the closing of the polls on election day, whichever occurs first' (polls close 7 p.m. MST -> 8 p.m. MST). Starting in 2026, early ballots delivered without qualifying identification must be signature verified.
'Unofficial election results are posted at 8pm on Election Day and are updated daily until all ballots have been tabulated.' Results are not official until canvassed.

'The first results – posted at 8:00 PM on Election Night' include early ballots already tabulated (signature verified). More results are added as memory drives return from voting locations; in-person Election Day voters usually make up 10-15% of the total vote. Ballots returned on Election Day ('late earlies') are valid if returned by 7 PM.

On-site tabulator results posted 'after 8 p.m. on Election Day'; 'it is standard for the final posting of ballots cast on Election Day to occur after midnight.' If all ballots arrived at once, counting would take '11 – 12 days for the General.' Goal: 100% of valid ballots not needing curing counted and reported 'by the end of day on the Thursday after the cure period ends on November 12, 2026.' Automatic recount window if needed: ~Nov 19 - Dec 4, 2026.

Elections Director Scott Jarrett to the Board of Supervisors: 'our goal is to have upwards of 99% of our ballots reported by the Friday after Election Day' (Fri Nov 6, 2026); 100% not possible by then because of the five-day cure period. In 2024 about 84% were counted by that Friday.

All ballots must be received by 7:00 p.m. (Arizona time) on Election Day; drop boxes open until 7:00 p.m. Nov 3. New process lets voters show valid ID at a Vote Center on Election Day to get the envelope 'ID Verified' and 'bypass Signature Verification.' Signature cure deadline: 5:00 p.m. on November 8, 2026.

'Maricopa County Elections will release the first batch of results at 8 p.m. on Election Night'; more results released through the night as memory cards reach MCTEC. Voters who show ID and tabulate an early ballot on-site 'will have their vote included in Election Night results.'

Votebeat: Maricopa ~23,000 voters (30% of Election Day drop-offs) and Pima 6,000+ (about half) used ID-verify; Maricopa finished signature verification ~8 a.m. the day after the primary and counted 99% of ballots by that Wednesday evening; Pima finished signature verification ~2 p.m. Wednesday. No official November forecast was given.

First results 'about an hour after the polls close'; Maricopa and Pima early ballots in the first round 'at about 8 p.m. MST'; 'New batches of ballots are usually reported each day'; state gives counties 'about two weeks to completely wrap up counting.'

No published general-election results-release schedule found. Pima's site lists Vote Centers open 6 a.m.-7 p.m. on Nov 3 and links a '2026 General Election - Early Ballots Processed (PDF)' and a live ballot-counting video feed; results page not yet updated for the general.

June 2026 primary precedent (NV SoS via FOX5): counties processed mail ballots 'received by Saturday... at 5 p.m. that were postmarked on or before Election Day, per Nevada law'; signature cure deadline the following Monday; county canvass on or before 10th day; unofficial results updated on Results.NV.gov. Clark County: general-election results 'available after 7:00 p.m. on Election Day'. No fixed daily update time published.

State law does not allow mail ballots to be opened and prepared for scanning until 7 a.m. on Election Day; 'Unofficial results will begin being reported on our Election Night Returns website after the polls close at 8 p.m. Nov. 3.' 'Counting takes time.'

Under a new state law, counties must release vote counts for most ballots by the 13th day after the election (signature-cure and some late-arriving VBM ballots exempt); counties have 30 days to finish; 'The frequency of updated results will vary based on the size of each county.' (Statements are for the June 2, 2026 primary; for Nov 3 the 13th day would be Nov 16 and the 30th day Dec 3 - computed, not announced.)

Absentee counting begins Election Night; early vote counted seven days after Election Day; absentees must be counted within 15 days; ranked-choice tabulation runs 'following the last counting of ballots on the 15th day following Election Day.' 2026 calendar: domestic absentee receipt deadline 11/13/2026, overseas 11/18/2026, 'Final regional count of Absentee and Questioned ballots' 11/18/2026 (so RCV tabulation on/after Nov 18 - computed), target certification 11/25/2026.

FairVote: in Nov 2026, the U.S. Senate race and the 2nd Congressional District use RCV (1st District does not). If no majority, ballots/memory devices are 'physically transported to the state capital of Augusta and counted there'; an RCV outcome could take about ten days. ME SoS: official results posted 'within 20 days after the election'.

MI SoS (Aug 2026 primary): clerks report unofficial results on their own websites election night; full unofficial reporting expected about 24 hours after polls close; absentee counting boards work into the night.
'preliminary election night results will not be released until 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time.'
